title: refactor(driver-sql): read the autonumber default from the contract, not a hardcoded fallback (#7263)
body:
Closes #7263. Execution half 3/3 of the maintainer's route-3 ruling on #6555.

## What changed

`{0000}` became a declared contract default in `@objectstack/spec/data`
(`DEFAULT_AUTONUMBER_FORMAT` / `resolveAutonumberFormat`, landed by #7265), so
driver-sql stops writing the default down for itself.

| Site | Final line |
|:--|:--|
| `sql-driver.ts` — import (symbol added to the existing `@objectstack/spec/data` import) | `:11` |
| `sql-driver.ts` — `initObjects` | `:5356` |
| `sql-driver.ts` — external-object registration path | `:5433` |

Both sites spelled the same four lines by hand; both are now
`const fmt = resolveAutonumberFormat(field);`. No new dependency — `@objectstack/spec`
was already in `dependencies` and the subpath was already imported. Site 2's `#1603`
comment about honouring both spellings is retired to the resolver's own docstring,
which carries it.

## Exactness proof

The review question here is narrow: is the substitution *exact*? A differential
harness ran the removed expressions and `resolveAutonumberFormat` over **484 field
documents** — both spellings across 22 value shapes (absent key, `undefined`, `null`,
`''`, non-empty strings, `'0'`, whitespace, numbers, `NaN`, booleans, arrays, objects,
a boxed `String`, `Symbol`, function, `BigInt`, null-prototype object).

**484/484 identical.** Including the cases the card asked to be proven rather than
assumed: `format: ''`, `autonumberFormat: ''`, both empty, `autonumberFormat: ''` beside
a real `format`, and non-string values in either key — all resolve to `{0000}` under
both old and new, and `DEFAULT_AUTONUMBER_FORMAT === '{0000}'` exactly.

One shape differs: a **`null`/`undefined` field** threw `TypeError` before and returns
the default now. It is unreachable — both sites evaluate `const type = field.type || 'string'`
several branches earlier, which throws on a null field before the autonumber branch is
entered. No behaviour change reaches a caller.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Eight driver-sql autonumber suites | **8 files / 64 tests passed**, unedited |
| `autonumber-seed-cross-side-parity.integration.test.ts` | **1 file / 5 tests passed** |
| Full driver-sql package suite | **81 passed / 4 skipped (85 files), 1156 passed / 48 skipped** |
| `typecheck` (`@objectstack/driver-sql`) | pass |
| `eslint` (touched files) | pass |
| changeset gates (empty / ADR-0087 / no-major) | pass |

No test was weakened: no case deleted, no assertion loosened, no retry, no `skip`. The
only test-file change is the one bounded prose exception — `sql-driver-autonumber-suffix.test.ts`
`:167-173`, comment-only (mechanically verified: every changed line in that file starts
with `//`). It re-points at the declared default and **keeps** its note that the engine
still emits a bare `11`, which stays true until #7262.

## Reverse verification

Three faults injected at both call sites, predictions stated before measuring:

| Fault | Predicted | Measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** — default dropped (undeclared → `''`) | 1 red: suffix `'11'` vs `'0011'` | ✅ exactly that — 1 failed / 63 passed |
| **B** — `format` shorthand branch lost | broad red, ~7 of 8 files | ⚠️ **8 of 8 files**, 45 failed / 19 passed |
| **C** — truthiness rule → bare `typeof` (the engine's `??`) | **no red** — no suite declares `format: ''` | ✅ 8 files / 64 tests still passed |

Fault B was redder than predicted: my survey grep missed the ES6 shorthand
`{ type: 'autonumber', format }` in the suffix helper, so all eight suites exercise the
shorthand spelling, not seven. The fixture was wrong, not the code.

Fault C is the load-bearing result: the subtlest wrong substitution — the one that
differs from the driver's rule *only* on the empty string — leaves all 64 tests green.
The suites cannot see that case, which is exactly why the exactness claim rests on the
484-document harness rather than on the suite.

## Not in this PR

The engine half is #7262 (engine-core); `applyAutonumbers` and `packages/objectql` are
untouched. #6555 stays open until both halves land.
